Definition: neuter of a derivative of G1142; a dæmonic being; by extension a deity:--devil, god.
BiblicalUsage: Demons fill the Gospels, and this is the ordinary word for them: unclean spirits that possess, torment, and speak, yet always yield to Jesus. He casts them out with a word, gives His disciples authority over them, and the demons themselves confess that He is the Son of God. Paul warns that the things the Gentiles sacrifice are offered to demons, not to God, and Revelation pictures fallen Babylon as a haunt of demons.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the New Testament is sober about demons: they are real, they are hostile, and they are defeated. I hold that no believer needs to fear them, because the One who cast them out lives in us, and the demons know it.
RelatedEvents: Jesus Heals the Gerasene Demoniac; The Healing of the Demon-Possessed Boy
